sentence: This project builds cell models of digestive and liver disease by editing genes in cell lines and stem cells.
This project tests whether one enzyme disrupts macrophages during metabolic disorders and contributes to atherosclerosis caused by diet.
This project tests whether an injectable hydrogel scaffold activated by ultrasound can help cartilage heal in osteoarthritis.
This project studies how glioma driver mutations change RNA splicing and tests whether targeting RNA splicing can treat gliomas.
This project builds a method for computers to learn connections between genes from tissues with lots of data, to map gene networks disrupted in cardiovascular disease.
This project studies how phosphorylation controls the way proteins work and are organized inside cells.
This project studies how sex differences affect the brain circuits behind contextual memories linked to cocaine.
This project uses spatial functional genomics to study how tumor gene changes and age-related changes around the tumor affect the response to immunotherapy.
This project uses genetic data from many people to study how complex traits evolved and to find genetic variants linked to disease.
This project studies how stress and an autism-linked gene change affect the striatal circuits that control habits.
This project studies non-canonical antigens in lung cancer and how cells present them.
This project builds statistical and computational methods to work out what common non-coding variants do in complex diseases.
This project tests whether waves of electrical activity called cortical spreading depolarizations affect the hippocampus after traumatic brain injury.
This project tests whether antigen on the lining of blood vessels can guide expanded T cells to the right sites and how to make this work better.
This project studies how a substance passed from mother to fetus during pregnancy protects newborns from allergy.
This project coordinates and supports research projects that use stem cell approaches to understand and treat lung diseases.
This project compares two treatments to find how well they kill Stenotrophomonas maltophilia and prevent resistance.
This project provides single cell genomics services and intestinal organoid cultures so researchers can study gut disease and repair.
This project combines recordings from human auditory cortex with computational modeling to find how the brain recognizes speech across different sound conditions.
This project builds a vector system that delivers antigens to immune cells to develop immunotherapies for cancer.
